rotate-pdf.formula:
new_rotation = (current_rotation + chosen_angle) mod 360

Angles are stored per page in the PDF. Example: a page at 90° rotated by 270° → (90 + 270) mod 360 = 0° (upright).
howTo: Upload one or more PDF files (up to 50 MB each).
Pick the rotation angle: 90°, 180° or 270° clockwise.
Optionally type page ranges per file (e.g. 1,3,5-8); leave empty for all pages.
Click rotate to apply the new orientation.
Download the fixed PDF — or a ZIP when you rotated several files.
keyFacts: Pages rotate by 90°, 180° or 270° clockwise, applied to all pages or a chosen range.
The rotation is written into each page's /Rotate entry, so the fix is permanent in every viewer.
Multiple PDFs can be processed in one batch; several outputs are bundled into a single ZIP.
Page ranges use familiar notation: 1,3,5-8 means pages 1, 3, and 5 through 8.
Everything runs locally with pdf-lib — files up to 50 MB each, never uploaded.

limitations: Only 90° steps are possible — arbitrary angles like 37° are not supported.
Pages with existing rotation accumulate: rotating twice by 90° equals one 180° turn.
Scanned pages rotate as images; this cannot straighten a slightly skewed scan.
Password-protected PDFs that need a password prompt cannot be processed.
